Ut sit sensus : Ira enim viri, id est ira per vitium cujuscumque hominis, justitiam Dei, id est opus vere justum et Deo acceptum, non operatur, sed opus Deo displicens atque damnabile facit, quia a rationis tramite abducit, et contra justitiam agit. Iracundo quippe bonum et justum videtur, quidquid ab ira suggeritur. Atque, ut ait Gregorius, menti furore ebriæ, quidquid recte dicitur, perversum videtur. Et rursus : Per iram, inquit, sapientia perditur, ut quid, quove ordine quid agendum sit, nesciatur. Hinc Job : Non te ira superet, ut aliquem opprimas. Et Salomon : Ira non habet misericordiam, nec erumpens furor ; et impetum concitati spiritus ferre quis poterit ? Irascamur ergo propriis vitiis, et ea ulciscamur discrete in nobis. Irascere tibi quia ad iram irrationabiliter motus es, et cessa irasci. Et maxime qui vel ex usu maligno aut naturali dispositione ad iram proclives sunt, contra iram jugiter debent pugnare, et pro ejus exstirpatione studere, ac Deum infatigabiliter deprecari. Advertamus ergo quod ait Salvator : Beati mites ; et, Discite a me quia mitis sum et humilis corde.
paras.en: [[1:20|For the anger of man worketh not the justice of God|Ira enim viri, justitiam Dei non operatur]]. That holy Apostle speaks with restraint: for less is said and more is meant. So that the sense is: For the anger of man, that is, the vicious anger of any man whatever, worketh not the justice of God, that is, a work truly just and acceptable to God, but produces a work displeasing to God and damnable, because it leads away from the path of reason and acts against justice. For to the angry man whatever anger suggests seems good and just. And, as Gregory says, to a mind drunk with fury, whatever is rightly said seems perverse. And again: Through anger, he says, wisdom is lost, so that one knows not what is to be done, or in what order. Hence Job: [[Job 36:18|Therefore let not anger overcome thee to oppress any man|Non te ira superet, ut aliquem opprimas]]. And Solomon: [[Prov 27:4|Anger hath no mercy: nor fury, when it breaketh forth: and who can bear the violence of one provoked?|Ira non habet misericordiam, nec erumpens furor ; et impetum concitati spiritus ferre quis poterit]]? Let us then be angry with our own vices, and avenge them discreetly in ourselves. Be angry with thyself because thou wast moved unreasonably to anger, and cease to be angry. And especially those who, whether from bad habit or natural disposition, are prone to anger ought continually to fight against anger, strive for its uprooting, and pray to God untiringly. Let us heed, then, what the Saviour says: [[Matt 5:4|Blessed are the meek|Beati mites]]; and: [[Matt 11:29|learn of me, because I am meek, and humble of heart|Discite a me quia mitis sum et humilis corde]].

paras.t: Superbi siquidem ad iram sunt proniores : humiles vero mitescunt et patientes consistunt. Denique si ira subito oriatur, nequaquam perseveret in corde, quum in Ecclesiastico dicatur : Homo homini servat iram, et a Deo quærit medelam ? Quis exorabit pro delictis illius ? Insuper, locus iste etiam de ira per zelum potest exponi : quoniam etsi ira hæc commendetur, tamen per eam judicans aut ulciscens, a divinæ perfectionis tranquillitate et summi Judicis serenitate occumbit. Scriptum est enim de Deo : Tu, dominator Domine, cum tranquillitate judicas. Et alibi : Numquid ad iracundiam me provocant ? ait Dominus ; nonne semetipsos in confusione vultus sui ? Hinc asserit Beda : Judex homo, qui amissa mentis tranquillitate judicat delinquentem, etiamsi juste judicet, justitiam tamen divini examinis, in quam perturbatio cadere nequit, imitari non valet.
paras.en: For the proud are more prone to anger, but the humble grow gentle and remain patient. Further, if anger arises suddenly, let it by no means persist in the heart, since it is said in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 28:3|Man to man reserveth anger, and doth he seek remedy of God?|Homo homini servat iram, et a Deo quærit medelam]]? [[Ecclus 28:5|who shall obtain pardon for his sins?|Quis exorabit pro delictis illius]]? Moreover, this place can also be expounded of anger through zeal: for although this anger is commended, yet one who judges or avenges through it falls short of the tranquillity of the divine perfection and the serenity of the supreme Judge. For it is written of God: [[Wis 12:18|thou being master of power, judgest with tranquillity|Tu, dominator Domine, cum tranquillitate judicas]]. And elsewhere: [[Jer 7:19|Do they provoke me to anger, saith the Lord? is it not themselves, to the confusion of their own countenance?|Numquid ad iracundiam me provocant ? ait Dominus ; nonne semetipsos in confusione vultus sui]]? Hence Bede asserts: A human judge who judges an offender having lost the tranquillity of his mind, even if he judges justly, cannot imitate the justice of the divine examination, into which no disturbance can fall.

paras.t: Propter quod abjicientes omnem immunditiam, id est, pœnitendo seu præcavendo, de vobis expellite carnalia ac spiritualia vitia consueta : quemadmodum monet Apostolus, Mundemus nos ab omni inquinamento carnis et spiritus, perficientes sanctificationem in timore Dei ; et abundantiam malitiæ, id est graviora facinora, ut quæ ex consuetudine prava, ex deliberato proposito, ex pertinaci intentione nascuntur ; in mansuetudine suscipite, id est, mansuete et patienter audite, firmiterque tenete, insitum verbum, id est evangelicæ legis doctrinam, vobis a prædicatoribus insinuatam, impressam, infusam. Maturitas enim sapientiæ seu verbum salutaris doctrinæ, non nisi mansuete et tranquilla mente percipitur : a cujus salubri susceptione impedit ira. Idcirco in Ecclesiastico docetur : Esto mansuetus ad audiendum verbum Dei, ut intelligas. Nam ut communiter dicitur, Impedit ira animum ne possit cernere verum. Mansuetudo autem est quædam tractabilitas mentis, eam disponens ad susceptionem verbi salutis : quemadmodum tractabilitas ceræ, dispositio est ad impressionem sigilli.
paras.en: [[1:21|Wherefore, casting away all uncleanness|Propter quod abjicientes omnem immunditiam]], that is, by repenting or guarding against them, drive out from yourselves the carnal and spiritual vices you are used to, as the Apostle admonishes: [[2 Cor 7:1|let us cleanse ourselves from all defilement of the flesh and of the spirit, perfecting sanctification in the fear of God|Mundemus nos ab omni inquinamento carnis et spiritus, perficientes sanctificationem in timore Dei]]; [[1:21|and abundance of naughtiness|et abundantiam malitiæ]], that is, the graver crimes, such as spring from wicked habit, from deliberate purpose, from obstinate intention; [[1:21|with meekness receive|in mansuetudine suscipite]], that is, hear meekly and patiently, and hold firmly, [[1:21|the ingrafted word|insitum verbum]], that is, the teaching of the gospel law, instilled, impressed and poured into you by the preachers. For the ripeness of wisdom, or the word of saving doctrine, is received only with a meek and tranquil mind; from whose wholesome reception anger hinders. Therefore Ecclesiasticus teaches: [[Ecclus 5:13|Be meek to hear the word, that thou mayst understand|Esto mansuetus ad audiendum verbum Dei, ut intelligas]] [Denis's text adds *of God*]. For, as is commonly said, Anger hinders the mind from being able to discern the truth. Meekness is a certain tractableness of mind, disposing it to the reception of the word of salvation, as the tractableness of wax is a disposition for the impression of the seal.

paras.t: Quod potest salvare animas vestras. Nam verbum Dei instruit hominem de necessariis ad salutem, et ita instrumentaliter seu dispositive salvare dicitur hominem, si observetur et impleatur. Ideo dictum est : Beati qui audiunt verbum Dei, et custodiunt illud. Et Psalmista : Lucerna, inquit, pedibus meis verbum tuum, Domine, et lumen semitis meis. Alibi quoque fertur : Non nativitatis fructus pascunt homines, sed sermo tuus eos qui in te credunt, conservat. Cum omni ergo reverentia ac diligentia audiant subditi verbum Dei a superioribus suis ac sapientioribus. Hæc autem purgatio mentis necessaria est, quia oportet in primis a malo recedere. In malevolam enim animam non intrabit sapientia, nec habitabit in corpore subdito peccatis. Itaque puritas mentis est maxime appetenda, jugiter exquirenda, diligentissime conservanda : quia ut ait Salvator, Beati mundo corde, quoniam ipsi Deum videbunt; Salomon quoque, Qui diligit cordis munditiam, habebit amicum regem. Ideo cum Psalmista incessanter oremus : Cor mundum crea in me, Deus.
paras.en: [[1:21|which is able to save your souls|Quod potest salvare animas vestras]]. For the word of God instructs man in the things necessary for salvation, and so it is said to save man instrumentally or dispositively, if it is observed and fulfilled. Therefore it was said: [[Luke 11:28|blessed are they who hear the word of God and keep it|Beati qui audiunt verbum Dei, et custodiunt illud]]. And the Psalmist says: [[Ps 118:105|Thy word is a lamp to my feet, and a light to my paths|Lucerna, inquit, pedibus meis verbum tuum, Domine, et lumen semitis meis]]. Elsewhere too it is said: [[Wis 16:26|not the growing of fruits that nourisheth men, but thy word preserveth them that believe in thee|Non nativitatis fructus pascunt homines, sed sermo tuus eos qui in te credunt, conservat]]. With all reverence and diligence, then, let subjects hear the word of God from their superiors and those wiser than they. Now this purging of the mind is necessary, because we must first of all depart from evil. For [[Wis 1:4|wisdom will not enter into a malicious soul, nor dwell in a body subject to sins|In malevolam enim animam non intrabit sapientia, nec habitabit in corpore subdito peccatis]]. Therefore purity of mind is above all to be desired, continually sought, most diligently preserved: for, as the Saviour says, [[Matt 5:8|Blessed are the clean of heart: they shall see God|Beati mundo corde, quoniam ipsi Deum videbunt]]; and Solomon: [[Prov 22:11|He that loveth cleanness of heart|Qui diligit cordis munditiam]] shall have the king for his friend. Therefore let us pray unceasingly with the Psalmist: [[Ps 50:12|Create a clean heart in me, O God|Cor mundum crea in me, Deus]].
